summary:
Donald Trump threatened to “annihilate” Iran in his address to the UN General Assembly, while also saying he had a major decision to make. He said US officials had met an Iranian delegation for three hours; one account said Trump expected a deal after the US midterm elections. The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement permitting a larger US military presence on the island, with at least two new bases planned.

Sri Lanka’s High Court convicted 15 men accused of direct involvement in the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings, which killed 279 people and wounded about 500. Nine defendants were acquitted. In Japan, Typhoon Dujuan brought record rain, landslides and power outages; reports put the death toll at four and five. More than 74,000 people in the Tokyo region remained under evacuation orders.

British Columbia sued OpenAI, alleging the company could have prevented a school shooting by alerting police to the shooter’s ChatGPT use. The G7 demanded that Yemen’s Houthi rebels stop attacks on civilian shipping, as the UK offered time-limited defensive support to Saudi Arabia. A UN human rights investigator said US strikes on boats alleged to carry drugs may constitute crimes against humanity; dozens of attacks have killed more than 230 people, the Guardian reported.

headlines.title: Trump threatens Iran in UN speech while raising prospect of a deal
headlines.summary: Donald Trump threatened to “annihilate” Iran in his address to the UN General Assembly, while saying he had a major decision to make. He also said US officials had met an Iranian delegation for three hours; one account said Trump expected a deal after the US midterm elections.

headlines.title: US, Denmark and Greenland sign deal on expanded military presence
headlines.summary: The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement permitting a larger US military presence on the Arctic island. At least two new US bases are to be established under the deal.

headlines.title: Sri Lankan court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings
headlines.summary: Sri Lanka’s High Court convicted 15 men accused of direct involvement in the Easter Sunday bombings, while nine were acquitted. The attacks killed 279 people and wounded about 500, according to one report.

headlines.title: Typhoon kills at least four in Japan and brings record rain
headlines.summary: Typhoon Dujuan brought heavy rain, landslides and power outages to Japan, killing at least four people; another account put the toll at five. More than 74,000 people in the Tokyo region remained under evacuation orders.

headlines.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI over school shooting
headlines.summary: British Columbia sued OpenAI, alleging that the company could have prevented a mass shooting at a school by alerting police to the shooter’s ChatGPT use. The lawsuit also alleges gaps in the company’s product safety measures.

headlines.title: UK offers defensive support to Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
headlines.summary: The UK said it would provide time-limited, defensive support to Saudi Arabia as it counters Houthi attacks. The G7 has also demanded that the Houthis immediately stop attacks on civilian shipping.

headlines.title: UN expert says US strikes on alleged drug boats may be crimes
headlines.summary: A UN human rights investigator said there were reasonable grounds to believe US attacks on boats alleged to carry drugs could constitute crimes against humanity. The Guardian reported that dozens of strikes since September 2025 had killed more than 230 people.

headlines.title: EU removes two Russian oligarchs from sanctions list
headlines.summary: The European Union removed Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 others. Ukraine had argued the bloc should increase pressure on Moscow.
